issue_title: No way to set stock aside for a customer before billing
prompt:
Sales staff want to set stock aside for a customer who is still deciding, before any bill is raised. Today there is no way to do that: the only thing that ties up stock is a finished sale, so while a customer deliberates the same units can be promised to someone else and the business ends up over-committed. Add a way to put a temporary reservation on a quantity of a product for a customer, separate from raising a bill. While such a reservation is in place those units must not be available to anyone else, and there must be a way to let the reservation go again, returning the units to availability. Setting one aside must be all-or-nothing and must never set aside more than is genuinely available.

Implement this in the internal/service package: a HoldService constructed by service.NewHoldService(db). It must expose Place(tenantID, sku string, qty int, createdOn string) (Hold, error) - which reserves qty units of the product for the tenant and returns the created Hold (a struct with a string ID field), or returns an error without changing anything if qty exceeds the product's available stock (available = OnHand - Reserved) - and Release(holdID string) error, which frees that hold's units back to availability.

issue_title: Reservations never expire and can't be taken in part
prompt:
Now that staff can set stock aside for a customer, two gaps are causing problems. First, reservations are never cleaned up on their own: a customer walks away and their units stay set aside forever, slowly starving everyone else of stock. A reservation should be able to carry a cut-off date, and there should be a way to sweep up the ones whose time has passed and return their units to availability, while leaving newer reservations and ones with no cut-off alone. Second, a customer often takes only some of what was set aside. There should be a way to complete a reservation in part: the taken units actually leave the warehouse, the rest stay set aside for the customer, and once everything set aside has been taken the reservation is finished. Behavior for reservations that are not expired and not partially taken must be exactly as it is now.

Extend the internal/service HoldService with: PlaceUntil(tenantID, sku string, qty int, createdOn, expiresOn string) (Hold, error) - like Place but recording an expiry date; ExpireBefore(date string) int - release every hold whose expiry is on or before date and return how many were removed, leaving unexpired holds and holds with no expiry untouched; List(tenantID string) []Hold - the tenant's current live holds; and Fulfill(holdID string, qty int) error - take qty units from the hold so they leave on-hand stock, keep the remainder reserved, remove the hold once everything reserved has been taken, and treat an over-large qty as fulfilling the whole remaining hold.

issue_title: Invoice list pages drop invoices and shuffle their order
prompt:
Paging through a tenant's invoice list is unreliable. As users click from one page to the next, some invoices never show up at all - they fall through the cracks between pages - and the invoices do not come back in the order users expect. The trouble is worst right at the edges between pages, and when several invoices were issued on the same day their order jumps around from one viewing to the next.

Walking the list from the first page to the last should be a faithful, stable tour of every one of the tenant's invoices.

Invariants:
- The list has one definite, stable order, and invoices that look equal by the obvious measure still always come back in the same order.
- Following the pages from the start reaches every one of the tenant's invoices exactly once - nothing dropped at a page edge, nothing shown twice, and no stray empty page tacked on at the end even when the invoices divide evenly into pages.
- Only the tenant's own invoices appear.

Preserve existing public fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: A rejected invoice still leaves changes behind
prompt:
Operators report that a failed invoice leaves a mess behind. When they try to create an invoice that cannot go through - for example a customer's order asks for more of a product than the business has - the attempt is rejected, but afterwards the product looks partly committed even though no sale happened, a half-finished record can linger, and the next invoice they create skips a number as if the abandoned one had really existed. Sometimes an order is even let through that should not have been, leaving stock promised that the business cannot deliver.

Creating an invoice has to be all-or-nothing.

Invariants:
- A creation either fully succeeds or has no effect whatsoever; a rejected attempt leaves the business in exactly the state it was in beforehand.
- An invoice is only accepted when everything its customer is ordering can genuinely be fulfilled together, considering the order as a whole rather than each part in isolation.
- An abandoned attempt is as if it never happened, down to leaving no gap in how invoices are numbered.

Preserve existing public fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Service code is hard to maintain after a legacy import
prompt:
A previous import collapsed the invoice, inventory and reporting logic into a single catch-all package under internal/legacy (internal/legacy/legacy.go), with the unrelated concerns sharing terse internal names and a barrel file (internal/legacy/barrel.go) re-exposing them under their original public spellings. The service code has become hard to maintain and extend since that import.

Reorganize this logic into two clear, single-responsibility packages at the canonical layout the rest of the codebase expects:
- internal/service/invoices.go (package service): the invoice-creation logic together with the inventory/stock logic it depends on, exporting the public constructors NewInvoiceService and NewInventoryService and their types and errors.
- internal/reports/reports.go (package reports): the tenant revenue reporting and the by-status summary, exporting the public constructor NewService and its types.

The HTTP handlers under internal/handlers and the cmd/bizflowd entry point currently import internal/legacy; rewire them onto the new internal/service and internal/reports packages. The observable behavior and the public API must not change. Delete internal/legacy once nothing depends on it.

issue_title: Revenue report shows the wrong picture of what a tenant is owed
prompt:
Customers say the tenant revenue report (GET /reports/revenue) shows them the wrong picture of what they are owed. A business that just issued a bill and is waiting to be paid does not see that money anywhere in the report, so the amount outstanding looks too low. At the same time, figures occasionally show up that the customer does not recognise as their own, and cancelled bills they have already written off are still being counted as if the business expects to collect on them.

The report is meant to be an accurate, self-contained statement of one tenant's live revenue.

Invariants:
- The report reflects exactly the money this one tenant has invoiced and is still owed, and nothing belonging to anyone else.
- Money the business is owed but has not yet collected is part of the picture, not absent from it.
- A bill the tenant has cancelled is not revenue and has no effect on what the report shows or totals.

Preserve existing public fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Invoice status summary does not reconcile and mixes in other tenants
prompt:
The per-status invoice summary a tenant sees does not add up. Each row is meant to tell the business, for one status, how many of its invoices are in that state and what they come to in money - but the counts are wildly low, as if whole groups of invoices were being collapsed down to a single one, and the money figures are puffed up by invoices that belong to other businesses entirely. When a customer cross-checks the summary against their own books, the numbers simply do not match what they actually have.

The summary has to be a trustworthy breakdown of this one tenant's invoices.

Invariants:
- The summary describes exactly this tenant's invoices and no one else's.
- Every status reflects the true number of the tenant's invoices in that state, not merely that some exist, and only states the tenant actually has show up at all.
- The breakdown reconciles with the whole: adding the rows back together recovers the tenant's own invoice count and overall invoice total, with nothing missing and nothing extra.

Preserve existing public fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Inventory can be committed past what is actually in stock
prompt:
Inventory is being oversold. The business keeps committing units of a product that it does not actually have: reservations for a product go on succeeding even after everything in stock has already been promised, the reported availability does not fall as units get committed, and an order that asks for the same product across more than one of its lines can slip through even when those lines added together come to more than is left. Operators end up promising stock that cannot be delivered.

Reservations have to honour what is genuinely left to give out.

Invariants:
- A product can never be committed beyond what it actually has; everything already promised counts against what remains.
- The remaining availability the system reports always matches what is truly still free to reserve, and a rejected request changes nothing.
- Demand for the same product is weighed as a whole, so parts of one order cannot each look acceptable on their own yet together exceed what is left.

Preserve existing public fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Some CSV values come out garbled
prompt:
Users report that some rows of their CSV files come out garbled. When a value is wrapped in quotes so that it can hold a comma, the tool tears it into pieces at that comma instead of keeping it whole, and quoted values that contain an escaped quotation mark show up with stray extra quote marks in them. Plain values and empty values look fine; the trouble is with quoted values.

For example, a name field written as the quoted value "Smith, John" should stay a single field but currently breaks apart.

The parser is expected to honour the usual quoting convention end to end:
- A quoted value is delimited by the quotes that surround it, and the data inside those quotes (including any separators) belongs to that one value; an escaped quotation mark inside it reads as a single quotation mark in the result.
- The quoting convention only applies to a value that is actually presented as quoted; text that merely happens to contain a quotation mark is ordinary data and must be left exactly as written.

Preserve existing public types/fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: The tool runs out of memory on very large files
prompt:
Some customers now run the tool over very large exports - files far too big to hold in memory all at once - and the tool runs out of memory or grinds to a halt because it reads the whole file in before it computes anything. They need to point it at one of these large files and get the same column summary back without the tool trying to load the entire file first; it should be able to work through the input a piece at a time and keep only a running summary.

This has to keep working for the files that don't use commas between columns: when a caller has told the tool which separator their file uses, the piece-at-a-time path must read those files exactly the same way the normal path already does, and the summary it returns must match what the tool produces today for the same file and column.

Provide logforge::streamSummary(std::istream& in, int columnIndex, const Dialect& dialect, bool skipHeader), declared under include/logforge/, returning the same Summary type the existing summary uses. It must fold the stream one line at a time into a running Summary (count, sum, mean, min, max) for the given column, parsing each line with the supplied dialect and optionally skipping a header line, never loading the whole input at once, and must match the existing full-file summary for the same file and column.

issue_title: Report figures look untrustworthy
prompt:
The numbers in the printed report come out wrong in a few ways and users do not trust the figures.

First, the values look like they have simply had their extra digits chopped off rather than being turned into the nearest value at the precision asked for, so a figure that should tick up to the next value instead stays low.

Second, a figure that works out to nothing still shows up wearing a minus sign, so the report displays a signed zero where a plain zero is expected.

Third, in the summary block the smallest and largest figures are shown with fewer digits after the decimal point than the other figures beside them, so the columns do not line up consistently.

Figures that already sit exactly at the requested precision display correctly.

The report is expected to be trustworthy:
- A formatted figure is the closest representable value at the requested precision, with the usual tie-breaking, and a figure that amounts to nothing is shown as a plain unsigned zero.
- Every figure in the summary is shown to the same precision as its neighbours.

Preserve existing public types/fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Parser, statistics and formatting code is hard to maintain after a legacy import
prompt:
A previous code import left the parsing, statistics and formatting logic collapsed into a single catch-all source file (src/core.cpp) behind one bundled header (include/blob.hpp) that re-declares everything under short internal names in namespace lf, with the CLI and smoke tests rewired to include only that bundled header. This makes the parser, statistics and formatting code hard to maintain.

Reorganize the library back into one focused source file per concern: parsing under src/parser/ (line parsing and numeric-field parsing), statistics under src/stats/ (column reading, summary statistics and rolling means), and formatting under src/format/ (fixed-point formatting, column layout and the summary renderer). Expose each concern through exactly three canonical public headers under include/logforge/ -- include/logforge/parser.hpp, include/logforge/stats.hpp and include/logforge/format.hpp -- declaring the public symbols in the logforge namespace. Callers must include those per-concern headers rather than the single bundled header. The observable behavior and the public API must not change.

The canonical headers must declare: in logforge/parser.hpp the Record type alias, parseLine and parseDouble; in logforge/stats.hpp the Summary struct, summarize, numericColumn and rollingMean; in logforge/format.hpp formatFixed, formatColumns and renderSummary. Remove src/core.cpp and include/blob.hpp.

issue_title: Moving averages come out wrong
prompt:
The moving-average feature gives wrong answers. Users plotting a moving average notice that only the very first average looks right; from the second one on, the numbers drift away from what a moving average over their data should be. When they run the same moving average directly over a column of one of their data files, it is even more off: the very first reading in the column seems to be missing from the result, so the whole curve is shifted and one point short.

The moving average is expected to behave like a moving average:
- Each reported average is the plain mean of the consecutive run of readings currently under the window, and there is one average for every position the window can fully occupy.
- When the average is taken from a data column, it is computed over that column's readings in order, with none of the genuine readings dropped from either end.

Preserve existing public types/fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Summary smallest/largest are wrong for some data
prompt:
The summary's smallest and largest figures come out wrong for some data, and users with negative readings cannot trust the report.

When every reading is below zero, the largest figure is reported as zero even though not one of the values is anywhere near zero. Separately, when readings are pulled from a column of a data file, the report behaves as though the negatives were positive, so a column of below-zero readings is summarised as if all its values had been flipped to the positive side. Data made up of ordinary positive numbers summarises correctly.

The summary is expected to reflect the actual data:
- The smallest and largest figures are the least and greatest values that are genuinely present, whatever their sign, and a lone reading is both the smallest and the largest.
- A reading drawn from a data column keeps the value it actually has, sign and all.

Preserve existing public types/fields and unrelated behavior.

issue_title: Evaluation looks unrealistically good on multi-symbol datasets
prompt:
When a dataset mixes several symbols together, the train/test split behaves badly and evaluation comes out far too optimistic. Some symbols end up with no test data, or no training data, and a check that is supposed to catch ordering problems in the split never reports one. Each symbol should get a fair, realistic split of its own history.

Expected:
- Every symbol ends up with both training and test rows, sized by the requested test fraction.
- No symbol is trained on its own future: each symbol's training rows all come before its test rows.
- The split's ordering check actually flags an ordering problem when one is present.
- Ordering stays deterministic across runs.

issue_title: Evaluation reporting code is hard to extend after a migration collapsed unrelated logic together
prompt:
The evaluation reporting code is hard to extend after a migration collapsed unrelated logic together. The per-fill P&L and equity-curve metrics, the per-window return statistics, the transaction-cost model, and the report assembly all ended up tangled inside a few catch-all modules under marketlab/core/ and marketlab/util/, reached through an indirection layer that renames everything. Adding or changing one concern means touching that shared pile and the name mapping.

Reorganize this logic into clear, single-responsibility modules at these canonical paths: marketlab/backtest.py (net_pnl and the equity-curve compute_metrics), marketlab/metrics.py (mean_return, win_rate, max_drawdown_from_returns), marketlab/costs.py (the trade_costs model and its CostBreakdown), and marketlab/reports.py (build_report). Keep marketlab/__init__.py as the public entrypoint that re-exports the same API under the same public names. The observable behavior and the public API must not change.

issue_title: Backtest report doesn't reconcile with itself when costs are on
prompt:
The generated backtest report is internally inconsistent once trading costs are involved. For some runs the headline result, the equity curve, the trade table, and the cost figures don't agree with each other, and the costs don't line up with the configured settings. A reader should be able to check every number in the report against the others and have them tie out.

Expected:
- The headline result, the equity curve, and the trade table all tell the same story.
- The cost figures match the configured cost settings.
- The order of trades in the report is preserved.
- Existing metric names stay unchanged.

issue_title: Analysts can't get a period-by-period walk-forward evaluation report
prompt:
When an analyst evaluates a strategy over time, they want to see how it held up across successive periods rather than a single blended number. Today the toolkit can score a return series but it can't hand back a structured period-by-period walk-forward view that lists each window, summarizes them together, and can be printed as-is. Add a new, separate report for this.

Expose a function importable from the package top level as `walk_forward_report(returns, train_size, test_size)` that returns a dict with three keys: `rows`, `summary`, and `text`. `rows` holds one entry per evaluation window, in window order, each entry carrying `window` (its zero-based index), `test_start`, `test_end`, `mean_return`, `win_rate`, and `max_drawdown`. `summary` carries `num_windows`, `mean_return` = mean of the window returns, `win_rate` = mean of the window win rates, and `max_drawdown` = the worst window drawdown. `text` is the same report rendered as a printable plain-text block: a title line, a column-header line, one line per window, and a final aggregate line labelled `summary` in lowercase. This is a distinct new entry point from any existing single-number evaluation. A series too short for any window must return an empty `rows` list and a zeroed `summary`, not raise.

issue_title: Feature and label rows stop lining up after gaps in the data
prompt:
Rolling features and forward-looking labels end up describing different rows once the input has missing periods and the horizon is bigger than one. With simple, contiguous data everything looks fine, but with gaps the feature rows and label rows no longer correspond to the same underlying rows, and a feature can end up reflecting a value it should not have seen yet. Features and labels need to describe the same rows.

Expected:
- Each feature is based only on rows before the row it describes - never the current row or a later one.
- After the initial rolling window is dropped, the remaining features and labels still refer to the same rows.
- This holds for larger horizons and for data with gaps, not just contiguous data.
- Keep the existing tests passing.

issue_title: Build a small integer mini-language interpreter exposed as tbx.Run
prompt:
Build a tiny embedded mini-language interpreter for this Go interpreter project and expose it to guest programs as a standard-library callable named tbx.Run with the signature Run(src string) string. It takes the full source text of a mini-language program, runs it, and returns the program's printed output: the lines emitted by print statements joined with '\n' (newline), with no trailing newline.

Guest programs use it like:

    package main
    import ("fmt"; "tbx")
    func main(){ fmt.Println(tbx.Run("let x = 2+3\nprint x")) }

The mini-language (integers only in this stage):

- A program is a sequence of statements separated by newlines or semicolons (';'); blank statements are ignored.
- Two statement forms: `let <ident> = <expr>` binds <expr> to the variable <ident>; `print <expr>` evaluates <expr> and emits one output line.
- Expressions: non-negative integer literals, variables, and the operators + - * / with standard precedence (* and / bind tighter than + and -), all left-associative. Parentheses group and nest. Unary minus is allowed in any position (-5, 3 * -2, 2 - -3, -(2+3)). Integer division truncates toward zero like Go's int division (7/2 -> 3, -7/2 -> -3). Whitespace inside a statement is ignored.
- If the program references an undefined variable or fails to parse, tbx.Run returns a single line 'error: <msg>' instead of normal output; the exact message text is your choice, only the 'error: ' prefix matters.

Implement the interpreter as a clean, multi-file Go package of your own (separate files for lexing, parsing, evaluation, and so on). Discover how this project registers standard-library callables for guest code by reading the existing core stdlib, and register tbx the same way. The guest import path must be "tbx" and the callable must be "Run".
skills_tested: designing a clean multi-file interpreter package
recursive-descent expression parsing with precedence and associativity
unary minus in any position and truncating integer division
discovering and registering a stdlib callable

issue_title: Add strings to the mini-language: literals, concat, len, upper
prompt:
Extend the existing mini-language interpreter (exposed as tbx.Run(src string) string) by adding a string data type. Strings must integrate with the language alongside integers, and every numeric behaviour from the first stage must keep working exactly as before.

Add:
- String literals in double quotes: "hello". Inside a literal, support two escapes: \" for a double quote and \n for a newline.
- A type-aware + operator: integer + integer adds (as before); string + string concatenates; mixing an integer and a string is a type error. On a type error, tbx.Run returns a single 'error: <msg>' line (message text is your choice; only the 'error: ' prefix matters).
- print of a string outputs its raw character content, with no surrounding quotes.
- Two single-argument builtins: len(x) returns the length of a string as an integer, and upper(x) returns the string upper-cased.

The operators -, *, / and unary minus stay integer-only. Everything from the first stage (let, print, integer arithmetic with precedence and associativity, parentheses, unary minus, truncating integer division, whitespace handling, and the undefined-variable / parse-error reporting) must still behave identically, and integers and strings must coexist within one program. Keep the implementation a clean multi-file package and continue exposing it through tbx.Run.
skills_tested: threading a new value type through an existing lexer, parser, and evaluator
lexing quoted string literals with escape sequences
type-aware operator overloading and type-error reporting
registering builtin functions in the parser and evaluator
preserving carried-over behaviour while extending a language

issue_title: Add an integer-to-English-words speller: tbx.NumToWords
skills_tested: teens as unique words rather than ten-plus-units
hyphenation between tens and units words
composing words with single spaces and no "and"
handling exact multiples and out-of-range inputs
discovering and registering a stdlib callable

issue_title: tbx.RomanTo returns wrong numbers
prompt: tbx.RomanTo(s) is supposed to take an uppercase Roman numeral in the valid range 1..3999 and return its integer value, where a symbol that is smaller than the one immediately to its right counts as a subtraction (so "IV" is 4, "IX" is 9, "XL" is 40, "MMXXIV" is 2024). The subtractive cases come out too big: "IV" gives 6 and "IX" gives 11, as if every symbol were just added together. Please make it compute the right value.

issue_title: Finance needs invoice summaries to include manual adjustments.
prompt:
Some invoices need manual adjustments after checkout - a one-off surcharge or discount that finance applies by hand. Today those adjustments are nowhere in the finance summaries, so admin reports show the wrong amount still owed. Add adjustment-aware invoice summaries. Introduce an Adjustment record with a signed amountCents (positive is a surcharge, negative is a discount), a reason, and a createdAt timestamp, recorded against an order. Then expose an invoice summary, one row per invoice, with the fields orderId, grossCents, adjustmentsCents, paidCents and dueCents, such that grossCents + adjustmentsCents - paidCents equals dueCents. Invoices that have no adjustments must behave exactly as before, and the existing admin report fields must be preserved.

Wire the feature through the existing dependency Container (app/Container.php) so it can be driven programmatically, using these exact public names: a Container property `adjustmentService` whose method `add($orderId, $amountCents, $reason)` records and returns the Adjustment; a Container property `adjustmentsRepo` whose method `findByOrder($orderId)` returns the recorded Adjustment objects for that order (each object exposing public `amountCents`, `reason`, and `createdAt`); and an `App\Services\InvoiceService` method `summary()` that takes no arguments and returns an array with one row per invoice carrying the fields named above.

issue_title: Retrying checkout after a failed payment shows a stale pending order
prompt: Customers who retry checkout after a failed payment sometimes see a stale pending order or a duplicate invoice. Retrying checkout should keep the cart stable, avoid duplicate invoices, and allow a fresh payment attempt when needed.

issue_title: Some accepted transactions show as unpaid in admin reports
prompt: One provider's accepted transactions sometimes show as unpaid. Normalise incoming gateway events so both providers' payloads are understood. GatewayEventNormalizer::normalize(string $provider, array $payload) must return an array with exactly the keys provider, eventId, paymentReference, status, amountCents, and currency. Both the older and newer Stripe-style and PayFast-style fixture payloads must be supported, status casing must be canonicalised to the documented values, amounts must be integer cents, and signature verification must remain enforced before any state change.

issue_title: Payment provider code is hard to maintain after a legacy import
prompt:
A previous legacy import left the payment-provider code flattened into a few unclear catch-all files (for example app/legacy/z_provider.php, app/legacy/a.php, app/legacy/b.php, and app/misc/pay_ops.php), each mixing several provider concerns together. The checkout and webhook flows still work, but the provider-specific logic is painful to maintain.

Reorganize the provider code into clear payment modules at these canonical paths: app/Payment/GatewayInterface.php (the gateway contract), app/Payment/StripeMockGateway.php and app/Payment/PayFastMockGateway.php (the two provider gateways), app/Payment/WebhookVerifier.php (signature verification), and app/Payment/GatewayEventNormalizer.php (provider payload normalization). Payment orchestration must remain under app/Services/, public/index.php must remain the entrypoint, and the existing checkout, webhook, and admin report behavior must not change.

issue_title: Customers need scheduled recurring payment attempts.
prompt:
Customers want to save an order and have it billed automatically on a regular cadence instead of checking out by hand each time. Add recurring payment schedule support for saved customer orders. A schedule must produce deterministic upcoming payment attempts without ever calling a real gateway: the caller passes in the current date and the system decides which schedules are due. Add a RecurringSchedule with customerId, amountCents, currency, intervalDays, nextRunAt, and status, and a service method generateDueAttempts($today) that returns the attempts due as of the given day. Preserve the existing one-time checkout behavior exactly.

Wire the feature through the existing dependency Container (app/Container.php) using these exact public names. Expose a Container property `recurringService` with: `createSchedule($customerId, $amountCents, $currency, $intervalDays, $startDate)` which creates and returns a RecurringSchedule (the returned object exposes public `id`, `customerId`, `amountCents`, `currency`, `intervalDays`, `nextRunAt`, and `status`); and `generateDueAttempts($today)` which returns an array of due attempt objects, each exposing public `id`, `scheduleId`, `amountCents`, and `currency`, and which advances each generated schedule's `nextRunAt` by its interval. Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` strings; `$startDate`/`$today` are passed in (no wall-clock). Define an `App\Domain\RecurringSchedule` class with a settable `status` property and the constants `RecurringSchedule::STATUS_ACTIVE` and `RecurringSchedule::STATUS_INACTIVE` (inactive schedules are never due). Expose a Container property `recurringSchedules` (the schedule store) with methods `saveSchedule($schedule)` that persists a modified schedule, `findSchedule($scheduleId)` that returns the stored RecurringSchedule for an id (or null), and `allAttempts()` that returns every generated attempt object.

issue_title: Recurring payments need pause, resume, and failed-payment recovery.
prompt:
Recurring schedules now need to survive failures. Support pausing a schedule after repeated failed payment attempts, resuming it manually, and retrying a failed attempt without ever duplicating a charge. Add pauseSchedule and resumeSchedule behavior; track failed attempts; and make retry create a new attempt only when it is appropriate (idempotent). A schedule that fails three times in a row pauses itself automatically. Keep the existing Stage 1 schedule behavior unchanged.

Extend the existing Container property `recurringService` (from the previous change) with these exact public methods, all keyed by id: `pauseSchedule($scheduleId)` (a paused schedule yields no due attempts from generateDueAttempts), `resumeSchedule($scheduleId)` (restores due generation), `markAttemptFailed($attemptId)` (records the failure and increments the schedule's failure count), and `retryAttempt($attemptId)` (creates at most one new attempt for a failed attempt; calling it again for the same attempt is idempotent and creates no duplicate). The RecurringSchedule object must expose a public `failureCount` property and an `isPaused()` method, and must auto-pause once its failure count reaches three. The existing Stage 1 entry points (`createSchedule(...)`, `generateDueAttempts($today)`, `recurringSchedules->saveSchedule($schedule)`) and their object shapes remain unchanged.

issue_title: Refunded payments do not always update the customer invoice
prompt: Finance sees refund records in the payment log, but invoice balances and order status sometimes remain stale. Make refunds update the customer-facing balances and status consistently.

issue_title: Admin payment reports disagree with invoice balances
prompt: Finance has seen completed orders where the payment list, invoice status, and order balance do not agree. Fix the reporting behaviour so the figures reconcile, while preserving the existing admin response fields.

issue_title: Payment flow changes are risky because unrelated logic is bundled together.
prompt:
Payment flow changes are risky because unrelated logic is bundled together. A previous legacy import flattened the checkout, provider-notification (webhook), and refund flows into a couple of catch-all files (app/legacy/flow.php and app/legacy/actions.php), each mixing several unrelated responsibilities. The flows still work, but touching one concern means reading through all of them.

Reorganize the code around clear service responsibilities, with controllers as thin request/response boundaries. The orchestration belongs in services at these canonical paths: app/Services/CheckoutService.php (checkout orchestration), app/Services/WebhookService.php (webhook handling), and app/Services/RefundService.php (refund handling). The request/response actions belong in thin controllers at app/Controllers/CheckoutController.php, app/Controllers/WebhookController.php, and app/Controllers/RefundController.php. public/index.php must remain the entrypoint and the existing public request behavior (checkout, webhooks, refunds, admin report) must not change.

issue_title: Retried provider notifications can update an order more than once
prompt: The payment provider may resend notifications. Retried notifications should not duplicate payments or move an order through its state more than once. Notification verification must stay enforced.

issue_title: Finance summaries don't reflect manual invoice adjustments
prompt: Finance sometimes applies a manual adjustment to an invoice - a one-off surcharge or discount that is not a payment or a credit memo. Right now those adjustments do not show up anywhere in the invoice totals or the by-status summary, so the amount a customer still owes is wrong whenever an adjustment has been made. Make adjustments part of the reported balances and the per-status summary, without changing the existing summary field names or the behavior for invoices that have no adjustments.

issue_title: Refunds aren't reflected in customer balances
prompt: When the business refunds money to a customer, that refund needs to be reflected in the same invoice balances and summaries that already account for manual adjustments. Today a refund leaves the reported balance looking as though the customer still paid in full, so the outstanding amount is understated. Fold refunds into the reported balances and the per-status summary, keeping the existing summary fields and the current behavior for invoices without refunds.

After a recent backend change, some invoice reports fail or show missing amounts and blank customer names, while reports built from older saved data still need to work. The failures show up when a single report mixes invoices that were saved before and after the change. Make the reporting flow handle invoices from either era - including batches that mix both - so amounts and customer names always come through, without changing the fields the rest of the app reads downstream, and without crashing when an invoice has no customer.

issue_title: Invoices land in the wrong day's report in some time zones
prompt:
The invoice date-range report puts some invoices on the wrong day. An invoice dated near the start or end of a day can fall into the wrong report depending on a customer's time-zone offset, and the last day of a range is sometimes included and sometimes left out. Invoices should be grouped by their local business day.

Expected:
- Invoices are compared by their local calendar day, using the offset provided (in minutes).
- The last day of the requested range is included.
- Results do not depend on the machine's own time zone.
- The caller's data is not modified.

issue_title: CSV export doesn't match the invoice report on screen
prompt:
After a filter is applied, the dashboard table, the CSV export, and the totals can disagree. Users report that the exported file is missing rows that are plainly in the filtered view, that some invoices show a blank amount in the export, and that the order of their own invoice list changes after they run an export. The export should faithfully represent the full filtered result.

Expected:
- The export contains the same filtered rows the user sees on screen, not just the current page.
- Every invoice shows its amount in the export.
- Running an export does not change the caller's original invoice list.
- Existing output fields stay unchanged.

A previous code import left the invoice and reporting logic collapsed into a few catch-all files under src/ (for example src/m1.js, src/m2.js, src/m3.js, src/m4.js, and src/lib/z.js), each mixing several unrelated concerns. This makes the billing code painful to change safely.

Keep src/index.js as the public entrypoint that re-exports the same API. The observable behavior and the public API must not change.

issue_title: Outstanding totals in the invoice summary are too high
prompt:
The invoice status summary overstates how much customers still owe. For accounts that have made payments or received adjustments, the outstanding figure doesn't match what the underlying invoices actually come to, and in some cases it moves in a direction that shouldn't be possible. Each status's totals should reconcile with the invoices grouped under it.

Expected:
- For every status, the summary's amounts agree with the invoices in that status.
- The amount still owed is never an impossible value.
- Keep the existing status labels and summary field names exactly as they are.
- Don't modify the caller's invoice data.

issue_title: Math.formatBytes prints the wrong sizes
prompt: This build adds a helper Math.formatBytes(n: number): string that formats a byte count human-readably using 1024-based units. The rule it should follow: pick the largest unit (B, KB, MB, GB) whose 1024-power fits in the value, divide the value by that 1024-power, and print the result with the unit. Bytes have no decimal places; KB/MB/GB are rounded to one decimal place, so e.g. 512 -> "512 B", 1536 -> "1.5 KB", 1610612736 -> "1.5 GB". Something is wrong at the unit boundaries: 1024 prints as "1024 B" instead of "1 KB", and 1048576 prints in KB instead of "1 MB". Figure out what is going on and fix it so formatBytes picks the right unit.

issue_title: Implement a small interpreted mini-language, exposed as Math.run(src)
prompt:
Add a new capability to this TypeScript runtime: a tiny interpreted mini-language, exposed through one built-in method Math.run(src: string): string. The argument is the source text of a mini-language program; the return value is that program's printed output.

The mini-language (this stage is numeric only):
- A program is a sequence of statements separated by newlines or ';'. Two statement forms exist:
    let <ident> = <expr>   binds a variable to the value of an expression
    print <expr>           evaluates the expression and emits one output line
- Expressions support: integer and decimal number literals; the operators + - * / with standard precedence (* and / bind tighter than + and -) and left-associativity (so 10-3-2 is 5 and 8/4/2 is 1); parentheses for grouping, with arbitrary nesting; unary minus in any position (-5, -(2+3)); and references to variables bound earlier with let. Whitespace between tokens is insignificant.
- Numbers are JavaScript numbers: division is real/floating (7/2 is 3.5), and integer-valued results print with NO decimal point (6/2 prints as 3, not 3.0).
- Math.run returns the print lines joined by a single '\n', with no trailing newline. A program with no print statements returns the empty string.
- Error handling: if the source cannot be parsed, or an expression references an undefined variable, Math.run returns exactly one line, 'error: <message>', and no program output. Choose clear, stable messages (their exact wording is part of the contract you define, so keep it deterministic).

The feature does not exist yet. Design it as a clean, multi-file subsystem (lexer, parser, AST, evaluator, and so on are separate concerns) rather than one monolithic function, and discover how this runtime registers built-ins so that console.log(Math.run("let x = 2 + 3 * 4; print x")) prints 14.
skills_tested: designing a multi-file interpreter subsystem from scratch
implementing a recursive-descent expression parser with precedence and associativity
tree-walking evaluation with a variable environment
JavaScript-style number formatting and real division
discovering an undocumented built-in registration mechanism in an unfamiliar codebase

issue_title: Add strings to the mini-language: literals, concatenation, len, upper
prompt:
Building on the existing Math.run mini-language (the numeric let/print interpreter from the previous stage), add a string data type. All existing numeric behavior must keep working unchanged.

Add:
- String literals in double quotes, e.g. "hello". Support exactly two escape sequences inside them: \" for a literal double-quote character and \n for a newline character.
- Overload the + operator: number + number still adds; string + string concatenates; mixing a number and a string in a + (in either order) is a type error.
- print of a string emits the raw string content (no surrounding quotes), so print "hi" outputs the line hi.
- Two string builtins, callable with function-call syntax: len(x) returns the length of string x as a number (usable in further arithmetic), and upper(x) returns x uppercased.

Report a type error (e.g. number + string) the same way the language already reports errors: Math.run returns a single 'error: <message>' line instead of any program output. Everything from the numeric stage must still hold: operator precedence and left-associativity, parentheses and nesting, unary minus, real division with JavaScript-style integer formatting, multi-statement output joined by newlines, and the undefined-variable / parse-error behavior. Integrate strings into the existing subsystem rather than building a separate path.
skills_tested: threading a new value type through every layer of an existing interpreter (lexer, parser, AST, values, evaluator)
lexing quoted string literals with escape sequences
type-aware operator overloading and type-error reporting
adding builtin functions with call syntax to an expression language
preserving existing numeric behavior while extending the value model

issue_title: Add a base-conversion helper: Math.toBase(n, base)
prompt:
Add a new built-in to this TypeScript runtime: Math.toBase(n: number, base: number): string. It takes an integer n and a base, and returns the string representation of n written in that base.

The contract it must satisfy:
- The base is an integer from 2 to 16 inclusive.
- Digits are written using the characters 0-9 for values 0 through 9, then the lowercase letters a-f for values 10 through 15.
- n is an integer; you do not need to handle fractional parts.

Worked examples:
- Math.toBase(255, 16) returns "ff"
- Math.toBase(10, 2) returns "1010"
- Math.toBase(100, 8) returns "144"

The feature does not exist yet; you are adding it from scratch. Figure out where and how this runtime registers its built-in Math members and wire Math.toBase in so that console.log(Math.toBase(255, 16)) prints ff.
skills_tested: implementing integer-to-string base conversion from scratch
mapping digit values above 9 to lowercase a-f
handling negative values as sign plus magnitude, and zero as a special case
discovering an undocumented built-in registration mechanism in an unfamiliar codebase

issue_title: Users need note revision history.
prompt:
Users need note revision history. Add revision history for notes so that, after saving, users can inspect previous content versions of a note. Expose three backend functions: save_note_revision(path, content) records the current content as a new revision; list_note_revisions(path) returns every recorded revision for a note; and get_note_revision(path, revisionId) returns a specific past revision. Each revision must be individually addressable by a stable revision id and must keep its content. Normal note save and load behaviour must continue to work exactly as before.

Implement these with the following exact Rust signatures and module paths (the public crate name is `vaultdesk`). In module `vaultdesk::commands::revisions`: `pub fn save_note_revision(store: &mut RevisionStore, path: &str, content: &str) -> Revision`; `pub fn list_note_revisions(store: &RevisionStore, path: &str) -> Vec<Revision>` returning the note's revisions in chronological order (index 0 is the oldest); `pub fn get_note_revision(store: &RevisionStore, path: &str, revision_id: u64) -> Option<Revision>`. Define `pub struct Revision` with public fields `revision_id: u64`, `content: String`, and `meta: RevisionMeta` (all clonable). Define `pub struct RevisionMeta` with public fields `byte_len: u64` (the content length in bytes when the revision was recorded) and `line_count: u64` (number of newline-separated lines, counting a trailing newline as terminating the final line, and 0 for empty content); the metadata is derived purely from the content, never from a wall clock. Provide the store at `vaultdesk::fs::revision_store::RevisionStore` with `pub fn new() -> RevisionStore`, `pub fn current_revision_id(&self, path: &str) -> u64` (0 when a note has no revisions), and `pub fn current(&self, path: &str) -> Option<&Revision>` (the latest stored revision for a note, or None); revision ids are monotonic per note starting at 1 (no timestamps). Keep these names, paths, and signatures exactly so existing callers compile.

issue_title: Revision history should protect users from save conflicts.
prompt: Revision history should protect users from save conflicts. When the same note is edited from two windows, a stale save must not silently overwrite newer content. Use the note's revision history to detect this. Implement, with these exact Rust signatures and module paths (crate name `vaultdesk`): in module `vaultdesk::commands::notes`, `pub fn save_note_with_revision(store: &mut RevisionStore, payload: SaveNotePayload) -> <result>` and a `pub struct SaveNotePayload` with public fields `path: String`, `content: String`, `expected_revision: u64`, and `overwrite: bool`. The returned result must expose public fields `ok: bool`, `conflict: bool`, `revision: u64` (the new revision id on an accepted save), and `current_revision: u64` (the note's actual current revision). A save whose `expected_revision` does not equal the note's current revision id must be rejected as a conflict (`ok` false, `conflict` true) and must not record anything, leaving the stored content and current revision unchanged, unless `overwrite` is true. An accepted save records a new revision (via the Stage 1 RevisionStore) and returns its new `revision`. A rejected save must set `current_revision` to the note's actual current revision so the client can re-sync. The existing Stage 1 revision-history functions, struct, paths and signatures (`vaultdesk::commands::revisions::{save_note_revision, list_note_revisions, get_note_revision}`, `vaultdesk::fs::revision_store::RevisionStore`) must keep working unchanged.

issue_title: Users need to tag notes and search by tag.
prompt:
Users need to tag notes and search by tag. Add note tagging so users can create tags, assign a tag to a note, remove a tag from a note, and search notes by tag, while keeping the existing text search intact.

The hidden harness compiles against the crate's public API by exact name, path, and signature, so implement EXACTLY this surface (no renames, no signature changes).

Rust tag store (a standalone in-memory primitive, re-exported at the crate root so callers can write `vaultdesk::TagStore`):
- `struct TagStore` with `pub fn new() -> TagStore`.
- `pub fn has_tag(&self, name: &str) -> bool` (true once a tag is created/assigned).
- It must expose enough to back the commands below; tag names and note ids are ordered so reads are deterministic.

Rust tag commands (free functions in `commands::tags`, re-exported at the crate root as `vaultdesk::create_tag` / `vaultdesk::assign_tag_to_note` / `vaultdesk::remove_tag_from_note`), with EXACTLY these signatures:
- `pub fn create_tag(tags: &mut TagStore, name: &str) -> bool` â€” returns true when the tag exists after the call; creating an existing tag is a no-op that still returns true.
- `pub fn assign_tag_to_note(tags: &mut TagStore, name: &str, note_id: &str) -> bool` â€” creates the tag on demand; assigning the same (tag, note) pair more than once is idempotent and still returns true.
- `pub fn remove_tag_from_note(tags: &mut TagStore, name: &str, note_id: &str) -> bool` â€” removing an absent pair is a no-op that still returns true.
- `pub fn search_by_tag(index: &SearchIndex, tags: &TagStore, name: &str) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (re-exported as `vaultdesk::search_by_tag`) â€” returns the notes carrying the tag.

The existing `SearchIndex` (re-exported as `vaultdesk::SearchIndex`) is constructed via `SearchIndex::new()` and populated via `index.add(id, title, path, content)`; the existing `pub fn search(index: &SearchIndex, q: &str) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (`vaultdesk::search`) MUST remain unchanged. `search_by_tag` must return the SAME canonical `SearchResult` shape and the SAME deterministic ordering (score descending, then id ascending) as `search`. `SearchResult` (re-exported as `vaultdesk::SearchResult`) is `#[derive(Serialize)]` with fields exactly `id: String`, `title: String`, `path: String`, `snippet: String`, `score: f64`, serializing to keys `{ id, title, path, snippet, score }` and nothing else.

Frontend (TypeScript): in `src/api/search.ts`, add and export `export function searchByTag(invoke: Invoker, tagName: string): SearchResultView[]` that calls `invoke("search_by_tag", { name: tagName })` and normalizes the raw list into the canonical `{ id, title, path, snippet, score }` shape (using the existing `normalizeSearchResults`). Keep the existing `export function searchByText(invoke: Invoker, query: string)` wrapper, which must still call `invoke("search", { q: query })`. The node harness imports `{ searchByTag, searchByText }` from `src/api/search.ts` by those exact names.

issue_title: Users need saved searches that can include tags.
prompt:
Users need saved searches that can include tags. Let users save a common search by name and re-run it later, where a saved query may combine free text and a set of tags. This builds on the Stage 1 tagging crate (TagStore, SearchIndex, search_by_tag, SearchResult).

The hidden harness compiles against the crate's public API by exact name, path, and signature, so implement EXACTLY this surface (no renames, no signature changes).

Rust query value (re-exported at the crate root as `vaultdesk::SearchQuery`): `struct SearchQuery` with public fields exactly `text: String` and `tags: Vec<String>`, `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]`, with these constructors used by the harness:
- `pub fn text_only(text: &str) -> SearchQuery`
- `pub fn tags_only(tags: &[&str]) -> SearchQuery`
- `pub fn new(text: &str, tags: &[&str]) -> SearchQuery`

Rust saved-search store (re-exported as `vaultdesk::SavedSearchStore`): `struct SavedSearchStore` with `pub fn new() -> SavedSearchStore`. It stores query definitions only (no cached results), so a saved search re-evaluates against the current index and tag state on every run.

Rust saved-search commands (free functions in `commands::saved_search`, re-exported at the crate root), with EXACTLY these signatures:
- `pub fn save_search(store: &mut SavedSearchStore, name: &str, query: SearchQuery) -> bool` (`vaultdesk::save_search`) â€” saves/replaces a named query; an empty name is rejected.
- `pub fn run_saved_search(store: &SavedSearchStore, index: &SearchIndex, tags: &TagStore, name: &str) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (`vaultdesk::run_saved_search`) â€” re-runs the named query; an unknown name yields an empty Vec.

Semantics: a text-only query behaves like text search; a tag-only query behaves like tag search; a combined query returns only notes that match the text AND carry every listed tag. Tag changes after saving are reflected on the next run (a removed tag drops the note). Results keep the canonical `SearchResult` shape and ordering (score descending, then id ascending), serializing to keys `{ id, title, path, snippet, score }` and nothing else.

Do NOT change the Stage 1 tag command results: `vaultdesk::create_tag`, `vaultdesk::assign_tag_to_note`, `vaultdesk::remove_tag_from_note`, `vaultdesk::search_by_tag`, and `vaultdesk::search` must behave exactly as before.

Frontend (TypeScript): note that this project runs under Node's native type stripping, so frontend imports have two hard requirements, exactly as the existing files do. (1) Every relative import between frontend modules MUST include the explicit `.ts` file extension. (2) Any type-only import (an interface or type alias such as `SearchResultView` or `Invoker`) MUST carry the `type` modifier, because type-stripping removes it from the runtime exports; for example `import { normalizeSearchResults, type SearchResultView, type Invoker } from "./search.ts";`. In `src/api/savedSearch.ts`, add and export `export function saveSearch(invoke: Invoker, name: string, query: any): boolean` that calls `invoke("save_search", { name, query })` with `query` normalized to `{ text: string, tags: string[] }`, and `export function runSavedSearch(invoke: Invoker, name: string): SearchResultView[]` that calls `invoke("run_saved_search", { name })` and normalizes the raw list into the canonical `{ id, title, path, snippet, score }` shape. The node harness imports `{ saveSearch, runSavedSearch }` from `src/api/savedSearch.ts` by those exact names.
